findings.title: Deleting a group throws UnsupportedOperationException when FGAP V2 is enabled
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener registers a ProviderEventListener (registered whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, which V2 implies) that on GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent calls management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). With the V2 feature enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose groups() method (added in this PR) returns GroupPermissionsV2, and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Provider events are published synchronously during group removal, so deleting any group with V2 enabled propagates this exception, fails the DELETE request and rolls back the transaction. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override groups(), so the V1 implementation handled the event without throwing. The V2 class should either implement the cleanup of the group's authorization resources/permissions or make these management methods no-ops instead of throwing on this path.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource UUID instead of the group id
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, the findByType callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with the resource name set to the group id, whereas Resource.getId() is the internal UUID of the authorization resource entity. Two consequences: (1) hasPermission does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing the resource UUID never finds the per-group resource and silently falls back to evaluating the "Groups" all-resource — per-group view-members/manage-members grants are never detected, or the wrong resource is evaluated; (2) the returned set contains resource UUIDs, but callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) store it in the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute / pass it to user-count queries that expect group ids, so user searches and counts for group-scoped admins are filtered by non-existent groups and return wrong (usually empty) results. The method should use groupResource.getName().

findings.title: Per-instance resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates per-instance resources (for a specific user, group, or client) via resourceStore.create(...) and updateScopes(...) but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the "all resources" created in init() get a type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates per-group resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...), so those resources are never returned there, and any type-based lookup/fallback in the policy engine will not see them either. The resource type should be set (resource.setType(resourceType)) when the resource is created.

findings.title: canManage() is satisfied by the view scope, allowing group management with view-only permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. an admin holding only the view scope on the Groups resource type is treated as able to manage groups globally. The no-arg requireManage() guards privileged operations — for example GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage() — so an admin with a view-only "all groups" permission can create top-level groups (privilege escalation). The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only the MANAGE scope; the no-arg variant should do the same. The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() in this PR also documents VIEW as sufficient and should be corrected.

findings.title: No upgrade path for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, so realms where fine-grained admin permissions V2 were initialized before this change never receive the new group scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) or the "Groups" all-resource. In such realms, creating a group permission fails at runtime: getScope() throws ModelValidationException("Scope [...] does not exist.") and getOrCreateResource() throws ModelException("No scopes found."), while GroupPermissionsV2's fallback getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups") returns null. A migration or schema-reconciliation step for existing resource servers is needed so upgraded realms can use the new Groups resource type.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for Groups resources
findings.body: getResourceName only resolves a human-readable name for the Users resource type; for every other type it returns resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created by getOrCreateResource. For a Groups-type policy the resource name is the group id, so permission listings in the admin console will render an empty/null resource name for group permissions. A GROUPS branch should resolve the group (e.g., to its name or path), or at minimum fall back to resource.getName() instead of the unset display name.
